title: RV / Homeland Guide
description: A simplified guide to progressing through the RV / Homeland portion of Aniimo
author: darksteelhyren

items.text: This is intended as a set-it-and-forget-it guide to each RV level. After you level up the RV, you come back, set up your base like I describe, then let it run until you have enough resources to upgrade the RV again.

Early on, byproducts from Trees and Mines are the limiting resource rather than Home Coins. This guide will maximize the amount of byproducts you get, so your RV upgrade will be available as soon as it's possible. Maximizing Home Coin gain is the second priority.

I will provide a text description of each RV level, occasional screenshots to help you understand, as well as optional notes and lessons you can read if you want to understand what's going on at each level.
Not all elements are created equal.

To put this simply, there are two kinds of task: 1) Things that run quickly, and 2) things that run slowly. There is no point optimizing things that run quickly; if a bread takes 60 seconds or 50 seconds to craft, that doesn't matter at all: we're still waiting 20 minutes for Wheat to grow.
Because of this, there are only two elements that DO matter:
Water. Increases how fast your Wells produce.
Earth. Increases how fast your Mines produce.
That's it! For the other elements, multiple coverages, even at low levels, is more valuable than high-level coverages.
This may change at higher RV levels. The guide will be updated to reflect this as the community moves to levels where, for example, electricity becomes utilized.

Press 5 in the Homeland. Look top-right. Press the (!) next to Ability Distribution. Your goal is to satisfy the recommended numbers, and make every number in the Ability Distribution green. While you're personally in the base, your Aniimo are much more efficient than they are when you're away or offline. Making the numbers green lets them continue at peak efficiency when you aren't there.
Shrubclaws (Basic Form), with Earth-3, Nature, and Transport, are very versatile. Remember that they should have "P"layful trait if you want to maximize RV level-up progress.
Glacy (Any Form), with Water-3, Ice, and Transport, are very useful.
Sherro (Thunderstorm Form) has Water-3, and covers electricity-2 nicely if you choose to use Aniipod Maker. Replace one of the Glacy.
Ignitis (Highland Form) provides Artisanship, Dark, Fire. Their evolution is a bit of a hassle. At low levels, _any_ fire Aniimo will do.
Gracewing (Night Form) provides Dark, Wind, and Leisure.
And, of course, you will want the family-specific Aniimo for their buildings, preferably along with the relevant trait (See Lesson: Traits)
The ideal choices for Aniimo change radically once you have your Crackle Generator.
Shrugclaws (Basic Form), with "P"layful. This, at least, doesn't change. Mines cost WWWAAAAYYYYY too much electricity to switch to E-mode.
Glacy (Any Form), with "F"aithful. My builds don't leave enough spare electricity to E-mode the Wells and keep them running at 120%. I recommend enough Glacy to power your Wells AND Cooling Unit.

Pomhawk (Basic Form) with "E"nergetic. The amount of Lumber you need to cut is almost absurd. Pomhawk was chosen because his alternate element doesn't risk tying him down to long-term production; we want him on call for Lumber.
Sparki/Flamerion/Sparkelf, equal to the number of Heat Furnaces you're running. Everything else that used to use Fire should be switched to E-mode.
Piopiota (Night Form) or Stellarys (Rain form). These will cover your Water and Dark needs.
Of course, you will still need to field specific Aniimo for buildings that require a member of a certain family.

Between some RV level setups, I will write down Lessons. They are things that I feel you might want to understand in order to understand why the build works, or perhaps an explanation of something you should be doing. I recommend reading them.
Follow the tutorial, and you should be well on your way to RV2 in no time.

There are a lot of traits. In the Homeland, traits do something different than what they do in the rest of the game. As a result, there's only a few that matter.
1) "P"layful; Increases Mine efficiency. This means you gain rock byproduct faster.
2) "F"aithful; Increases Well efficiency. This increases Home Coin gain, as you can produce more water.

3) "J"udicious; Increases Tidewhisper Sandcastle. This increases Home Coin gain, as you can produce more Salt. Starting at RV5, you should stock one Piopiota / Panpanta with "J". Starting at RV14, the sandcastle makes Pearls instead, and Pearls want the Shelly family: one Sherro with "J". Turbo/Dreaple use this trait in the Nimbus Bed starting at RV10. At RV16 the Nimbus Bed switches to Petals and wants an Iris-family Aniimo.
4) "I"nstinctive; Increases Dewy House efficiency. This increases Home Coin gain, as you can produce more Aromathyst. Starting at RV6, you should stock your base with one Fragrancier with "I".
Traits that reduce the times of fast tasks, such as Crafting Table or Carousel Mill, generally do not improve your throughput. They can be ignored until RV12 or so.

When looking at your orders, you can reroll them by clicking the circling arrows icon in the top right of the order.
Sometimes your order is just trash; very few Home Coins, or nothing besides home coins. You can consider rerolling them in this case.
Remember that orders, even so-called-"Urgent" orders, last until you complete them.
I recommend heavily rerolling orders to improve them. You get 5 free rerolls a day, and you can spend Home Coins for more. These costs don't go up with RV level.
You can luck into Urgent orders, but don't count on it; the odds seem really bad.
Or, you might get an order that gives Byproducts.
Or, you might get an order that gives (Pure) Element Gems, if you're after those.
In general, don't settle for crap orders.

Up until now, you've gotten Modification Toolkits from RV levelups. But you'll notice that once you arrive at RV7, you might be a little short.
From this point on, you're expected to obtain Modification Toolkits from the Index if you want to keep up.
In the Homeland, press 9, then on the lower left you'll see Index Score. Every time you collect a building, an item, or a decoration for the first time, you gain Index Points.
If you've obtained one of every craftable item until this point, you should be at or close to 1000. Try to get there shortly after starting RV8.
If there are any craftable items you haven't made yet, I encourage you to use rush items to obtain the materials for it, and then craft exactly one to get your missing Index Points.

Starting in RV7, some plants require temperatures. You will be given a heater and a cooler, both of which can be set to moderate or extreme temperatures. Some plants want Scorching, Warm, Cool, or Freezing temperatures, which you can provide with these two temperature buildings. Failure to do so will result in the plant taking longer to grow.

Upon initial inspection you may conclude that you cannot provide both Cool and Freezing at the same time (or Scorching and Warm at the same time.) However, if a plant is in both a Scorching and a Cool zone, it considers itself Warm. Likewise, if a plant is in both a Freezing and a Warm zone, it considers itself Cool. In this way, you can provide up to three different temperatures in your Homeland at the same time with only two temperature buildings.
This is slightly complicated, so for RV7 and RV9, I will provide a picture demonstrating the setup. The plants in the middle will be at their preferred moderate temperature.

Welcome to RV8.

You'll notice almost right away that you do not have ANYWHERE near enough Modification Toolkits to get all the components available. You didn't in RV7 either, but you had enough functional facilities to get to 1000 index points anyway.

Complete your RV quests so you get your house. Then press "9" in Homeland. You likely already have 1000 or so Index Points. I recommend that you bring that up to about 3000. And the way to do this is by purchasing decorations from the shop. You'll want ones that are as cheap as possible; grey-tier and green-tier are usually the best for this sort of thing; if it costs less than 15, just buy one.
Of special note are the blocks, which cost 2 Bud Tickets and provide 6 Index Points.
If you can't quite get to 3000, it's not the end of the world. Just be conservative with your component purchases until you NEED one.

Lastly, if you have the spare Aniimo, put shinies/prismanas in your house to generate Bud Tickets over time, which are used to buy decorations. Aniimo that are both shiny AND prismana generate the most. Remember to empty the jar occasionally.
Index Points goal: 3000. With this, you should have enough to buy every component available.

Lesson: Harvest Moon Festival Event
Take this section with a grain of salt.

There's a button on the top-right of your screen that becomes clickable at RV10, and you can do dailies to get "Moonray Wheat" coins. Use those coins to buy event seeds, grow the event crops, and fulfill event orders.
Do the dailies every day to get more coins.

In the same area, there's a shop where you can buy various recipees for Moonray Wheat coins (instead of spending those coins on more seeds). For now, I recommend purchasing the four recipees after you've done your first set of dailies.

I recommend cooking up any Event food that comes up in Orders, using Rush items to grow the needed crops. Maybe cook up 4 of each recipee? I don't recommend selling Event food in the Co-op shop, as it just sells for Home Coins.

As you grow Event crops and cook Event food, you aquire Harvest Moon Points, with rewards up to 160,000 Harvest Moon Points. At our current rate of Moonray Wheat coins per day, there's no way we can get to that point. I recommend stockpiling Moonray Wheat coins until the next phases of the event unlock. These will likely provide the proper ways to maximize our Harvest Moon Points.
More info to come.

You can free up bodies by turning various work stations on to e-mode, or electrical-mode.
Purchase the Power Module, then a Crackle Generator, and finally Crackle Power Poles as needed to extend coverage.

The Aniimo you use does not matter, the Crackle Generator is what produces the power. An Electricity-1 Aniimo does the same thing as an Electricity-4 Aniimo, just like with the heater and cooler. I recommend a Bolty.
If you don't use all the power, buildings produce more quickly, up to 120%. The more of the electric you use, the more you cut into that bonus. Going above the limit reduces work speed below 100%
Mines cost A LOT of power. DO NOT set mines to e-mode; continue to have "P"layful Shrubclaws utilize them.

You have access to a second Heat Furnace. Build it.
Set all processing buildings including Chimney Kilns and your level 2 Woodworking Bench to E-mode. Leave the Woodworking Bench handling Rough Lumber on Common mode.

Field one Nature-Artisan-3 Aniimo, such as Pomawk. Preferably it will have "E"nergetic. Wood Block byproduct processing needs have begun to be problematically high. This is the best non-prismana Aniimo to handle them, and at 360% efficiency, he works fast. This should carry us most of the way through our RV expedition.
Field one Electric Aniimo, such as unevolved Bolty, for the Crackle Generator.
As a result of E-mode, you no longer need a second Fragrancier for the Phonalfactory Table.

Do not set Wells or Mines on E-Mode. Cutting into the production speed bonus isn't a problem for processing buildings, but it is for Wells. Keeping Wells in Common Mode keeps them going at 120% speed.
You'll need to use the Sunlamp this time, for the Grapes and Walnuts.
